judgements.justification: B's oral came from its area chair's own reading, taste for 'a simple idea that works' and impact claim; no B reviewer rated above 8.
B's area chair predicted impact beyond BNNs, which no reviewer claimed, the paper does not test, and A never made.
f6JJ raised its B score after the response, while the same core response left every A score unchanged.
B's reviews averaged 3.6 hours against A's 6.0, mostly restated the paper, and Xxt6 gave 8 after 2 hours with no weakness listed.
Only A questioned why Fourier series beats other surrogates and asked for RBNN, and A's area chair kept both as required revisions.
Both committees saw the same simple, novel idea and the same missing ReActNet comparison but weighted them into poster versus oral.
B's oG66 raised to 8 'after reading comments from other reviewers', not citing the response.
A's FCVA gave 6 against wholly positive text, which lowered the mean that A's score-led area chair relied on.
No reviewer on either committee said they could not judge the paper; confidences were 4 or 5.
Neither area chair followed a single outlying reviewer; neither committee had an outlier.
The split came from B's area chair's own reading, not from a mean-based tiering of similar verbal verdicts; FCVA's mismatch is R08.
B's area chair cited own taste and an impact forecast for the oral, not the reviewers' unanimity.
Both committees received the same core rebuttal numbers, so B's raises did not rest on evidence A did not see.
The notes do not show B's meta-review dropping weaknesses its reviewers named; the main shared weakness was answered by the response.
The overstated Theorem 1 claims came from reviewers on both committees, so no one-sided factual error fed the split.
The response conceded no unfavourable result; it reported a +0.5 gain on the ReActNet recipe to both committees.
No reviewer raised a new objection or lowered a score after the response period.
B's area chair cited own reading and an impact forecast, not only scores, so the split is not a pure tier cut-off difference.
A's most expert reviewer (KUr5, confidence 5) had his Fourier-justification concern carried into A's required revisions.
KUr5 judged A's concerns addressed by the response, so A's scores did not stall on concerns no response could fix.
Neither committee had an outlying score; ratings were 8/7/6 and 8/8/8/7.
Neither committee had an outlying reviewer.
Neither committee had a detractor; A's area chair did not defend acceptance against a low score.
No reviewer or area chair raised audience breadth or venue fit.
The notes record no misstatement of reviewer positions or the response in either meta-review.
In A, oCAy never replied to a response that answered its ReActNet request and FCVA left no note, so pre-response scores stood while two B reviewers engaged and raised.
No reviewer on either committee said they could not verify the main results.
Neither committee split between accept and reject.
Both committees received the same core response; A's extra RBNN row and B's extra ablation number did not conflict.
No novelty verdict rested on a wrong account of prior work.
B's meta-review gave explicit grounds for the oral: own reading, taste and an impact forecast.
No reviewer contested the paper's framing from a neighbouring field's premises.
No reviewer on either committee rated above 8 or argued for a higher tier; B's reviews were light, not a close-reading champion.
Neither committee rejected the paper over the size of promised revisions; both accepted.
B's area chair based the oral on own reading, not on an off-record reviewer assessment; the off-record comments are not shown to drive it.
Both committees judged the paper as a method contribution by the same standards.
No reviewer held a below-threshold score; the lowest rating was 6.
